name: Siddhi Ganesh Temple
subtitle: A shrine of faith and new beginnings.
description: Dedicated to Lord Ganesha, this neighbourhood shrine is a place where devotees seek blessings for wisdom, prosperity and the removal of obstacles. It remains part of the everyday religious life of the area.

name: Koncha Dyo
subtitle: A tradition linked with prosperity and married life.
description: According to the local account shared for this report, an offering of alcohol is kept at the shrine and is believed to ensure that a household's prosperity never runs empty. The site is also said to hold special significance for married couples.

name: Mhepi Ajima — Mhepi Mandir
subtitle: A sacred hill where traditions meet.
description: This hilltop goddess shrine reflects the close relationship between Hindu and Buddhist traditions in Newar religious life. Its annual khat jatra keeps neighbourhood ties and ritual customs alive.

name: Nanak Math — Balaju
subtitle: A living connection to Sikh heritage.
description: Sikh tradition associates this sacred site with Guru Nanak's visit to Nepal. The Math is an important reminder of Kathmandu's religious diversity and the history of Sikh and Udasi devotional traditions.

name: Balaju 22 Dhara — Baisdhara
subtitle: Where water, history and devotion come together.
description: The 22 traditional stone spouts are commonly associated with the late Malla and early Shah periods. Their water heritage and the annual Baisdhara Mela make this a landmark of traditional engineering and living pilgrimage.

name: Pyatho Ajima — Sitalamai
subtitle: A mother goddess associated with protection.
description: Located within the Baisdhara complex, Sitalamai is worshipped in Newar tradition for the well-being and protection of children. The shrine becomes especially significant during the annual Baisdhara Mela.
